newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan group forms high-speed railway prep office.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan group forms high-speed railway prep office.

text.p: China Development Corp, a venture capital firm backed by the ruling Nationalist Party, said on Friday a group it leads has opened a preparatory office to bid for Taiwan's T$441.9 billion bullet train project.
The venture will have a paid-in capital of T$15 billion, of which China Development will account for 7.5 percent, the company said in a statement.
Other major investors include a Japanese high-speed railway consortium and the Taiwan firms BES Engieering, China Steel, Tuntex Distinct and Walsin Lihwa, each with 7.5 percent stakes, it said.
The team is one of two that signalled in January their intent to bid for the railway project.

While the China Development consortium will promote a Japanese high-speed railway system, the rival team, led by Continental Engineering, is promoting a European system with partners from France and Germany.

Taiwan formally invited tenders from local or foreign firms in October 1996 to finance and build the 345 km (220 mile) bullet train connecting northern Taipei and southern Kaohsiung along the island's industrialised western flank.
The winning bid will be selected by November 30.
Parliament adopted a bill in 1994 allowing private firms for the first time to invest in railway construction projects.
To encourage investments, the bill authorised tax incentives and state loans to private firms that work on railway projects.
The government hopes to attract 40 percent of the T$441.9 billion funding from the private sector.
